todays_goal: Connect camera optics to the human eye and correct the pinhole-camera misconception.

lessons.subject: science
lessons.previous_learning: Day 17 camera understanding was strong. One correction is needed: a pinhole image can be fairly sharp; its main trade-off is dimness because little light enters.
lessons.course_context: Apply the same light-path model to the human eye.
lessons.why_it_matters: The same optics explain cameras, eyes, microscopes, and other imaging systems.

vocabulary.definition: the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye
the clear front surface of the eye that helps bend light

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: a camera lens bends light toward a sensor. Your cornea and lens help bend light toward the retina. The retina detects light and sends signals to the brain.

worked_examples.title: Camera path
worked_examples.problem: How does a camera form an image?
worked_examples.explanation: The lens bends rays; the sensor detects them.

worked_examples.title: Eye path
worked_examples.problem: How does the eye form a visual signal?

independent_practice.prompt: What camera part is most like the retina?
Draw simple CAMERA and EYE light paths.

exit_ticket.prompt: Give one similarity between a camera and an eye.
exit_ticket.answer: Both redirect light toward a light-sensitive surface.

lessons.voice_prompt: Teach first. Compare CAMERA: lens -> sensor and EYE: cornea/lens -> retina -> brain on the whiteboard. Correct the pinhole misconception briefly. Keep questions short.
